ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High contrast ratio with an estimated 65% high-intensity (white) to 35% low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixel distribution across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Central and lower regions of both lobes consist of contiguous high-intensity white fields. Low-intensity dark pixels form a dense, irregular border along the trailing edges and appear as discrete, roughly circular clusters and mottled spots scattered throughout the white fields.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 50 degrees and a bounding-box depth extending significantly into the fluke midline.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency serration pattern along the entire continuous boundary; characterized by irregular peaks and valleys with a pixel-amplitude variation of approximately 5-20 pixels against the water background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The outer edges of both lobes follow a convex trajectory that transitions into a concave curve as it approaches the median notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High density of circular/annular dark pixel clusters ranging from 10-25 pixels in diameter, distributed across the high-intensity white regions, particularly concentrated on the left lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct, unaligned linear dark pixel disruptions are visible, notably a vertical-diagonal mark on the lower right lobe and several fine lines on the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive circular scarring across the ventral surface consistent with barnacle or parasite colonization; heavily serrated/notched trailing edge indicating cumulative physical wear.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly unique 'double-ring' or 'target' patterns where dark circular perimeters enclose white interior pixels, scattered across both lobes.
